890:
(a) If any charges herein provided for are paid in advance and garbage and yard waste collection service is discontinued or cancelled prior to the end of the period for which the charges are paid, a refund shall be made at that portion of the charges which is for the period subsequent to the discontinuance or cancellation of such service; provided, however, that no refund of less than one month's charge for garbage and yard waste collection service shall be made.
(b) Request for such refund shall be processed administratively under such rules and regulations thereof as shall be prescribed by the city or its contractor. Refunds may be granted as herein authorized only upon the written approval of the city or its contractor.
(Code 1989, § 11-69; Ord. No. 187, § 21, 9-20-1982)
891:
Refuse collectors are instructed to remove only the contents of the refuse containers. It is possible, however, to have a small amount of extra yard waste removed on the regular day of service for an extra charge, providing this material is placed in carton boxes and left next to the refuse containers. The city or its contractor shall be notified by the customer before the day of collection. The city or its contractor will determine the charge according to the amount of material to be removed.
(Code 1989, § 11-70; Ord. No. 187, § 22, 9-20-1982)
892:
(a) No person shall deposit for curbside pick-up any garbage, hazardous waste, inert trash or yard waste not contained within proper containers or otherwise properly prepared for pick-up in accordance with the requirements of this chapter. In addition, it shall be the duty of each person depositing specialized waste at the curb side to first make arrangements with the city's designated contractor for the pick-up of such waste. Specialized waste includes yard waste that is too bulky for authorized containers, large limbs and trees, inert trash, and other items which are not part of the regular garbage collection service provided by the city.
(b) Any person failing to remove or cause the removal of specialized waste or any garbage, yard waste or inert trash not in proper containers or properly prepared for removal within seven days after a written warning notice from the city requesting such removal shall be in violation of this chapter. Any person who is convicted of a first offense under this section shall be subject to a fine of $50.00. Any person who is convicted of a second violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of $125.00. Any person who is convicted of a third or any subsequent violation of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $500.00, nor more than $1,000.00, and each day that a violation occurs or continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(c) In addition, in the event that the occupant, owner or other responsible party fails to remove or cause the removal within the time specified, the city shall have the right to remove or cause the removal of such items at the expense of the owner and occupant, and the expense shall be added to and become part of the owner or occupant's garbage bill. In the case of rental property, whether single-family or multifamily, the tenant and the owner shall be jointly and severally liable for the cost of removal. In the case of multifamily fee simple property, the owner-occupant and the homeowners' association, if any, shall be jointly and severally liable for the cost of removal. If there is no homeowners' association, the management company, if any, shall be jointly and severally liable with the owner-occupant for the cost of removal. In the event that any removal fee remains unpaid for a period of 30 days after written notice, the city may pursue any and all civil remedies available to the city at law or in equity to collect the fee, and the city may, after an additional 15-day period of prior written notice, discontinue water and garbage service to the applicable property. The punishment or conviction of any person under subsection (b) of this section shall not relieve the person from paying any unpaid removal fee; nor shall payment of any unpaid removal fee bar criminal prosecution for any violation of this chapter.
(Code 1989, § 11-71; Ord. No. 400, § 1, 2-16-1998)
894:

895:
Commercial solid waste customers in the city are authorized to contract for commercial solid waste collection and disposal services from any contractor, provided that such contractor first obtains a solid waste collection permit from the city. Rates and other contract terms, including, but not limited to, container size and frequency of collections, shall be negotiated between the contractor and the customer, provided that such terms do not conflict with the provisions of this chapter or other applicable city ordinances.
(Code 1989, § 11-81; Ord. No. 354, § 1, 12-19-1994)
896:
It shall be unlawful for any commercial solid waste contractor (hereinafter "commercial contractor") to provide commercial solid waste collection and disposal services within the city without first obtaining a city solid waste collection permit. Contractors desiring to perform such services shall make written application to the city for a permit on forms prescribed by the city director of finance. All applications shall be accompanied by a $500.00 application fee to defray investigative, administrative and regulatory costs. Permits shall be issued to qualified applicants for the full calendar year, or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year, at the time the application is approved. Each commercial contractor issued a permit shall pay a quarterly permit fee to the city as provided in section 38-25. All permits granted under this chapter shall expire on December 31 of each year. Commercial contractors desiring to renew their permits shall file renewal applications accompanied by a $500.00 renewal application fee. The renewal application shall be submitted on forms prescribed by the director on or before November 15 of each year. In the event annual permit fees go unpaid after the due date, a ten percent penalty will be charged, based upon the past due amount. Further, a 12 percent per annum interest charge shall accrue until the permit fees are paid in full.
(Code 1989, § 11-82; Ord. No. 354, § 2, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 1, 4-3-1999; Ord. No. 505, 9-23-2002)
897:
(a) Each commercial contractor shall pay a permit fee to be set by the city council from time to time per cubic yard of solid waste removed from the city, payable in accordance with billing and reporting procedures adopted from time to time by the director. For the purposes of determining the permit fee, solid waste shall be deemed to include trash, construction debris, demolition debris, medical waste, yard waste and rubbish, inert waste, hazardous waste, and any other solid waste not covered under separate contract with the city. In general, the volume and weights of solid waste shall be based upon actual weights of containers. Where actual weighing is not done, the permit fees shall be based upon the sizes of the containers, the frequency of collection and the types of waste mix in the container. The director will provide the average weight factors to be used. For the purpose of fee calculation, all containers shall be deemed full at the time of each collection. On or before the tenth working day of the first month following the end of each calendar quarter, the commercial contractor shall submit a quarterly fee based upon the cubic yards of waste removed from the city for the immediately preceding quarter, together with a report providing such information as the director shall deem appropriate. In the event permit fees go unpaid after the due date, a ten percent penalty will be charged based upon the past due amount. Further, a 12 percent per annum interest charge shall accrue until the permit fees are paid in full. The report shall contain, but shall not be limited to, a listing of customers served during the quarter, together with the size of containers and collection frequency for each customer; total tons of materials landfilled and recycled by city customers; identification of landfills used by the contractor; and identification of end users of recycled materials. The report shall be submitted in written form. The director or his designee shall have the right to examine at any time commercial contractors' books, records and computer data relating to the removal of solid waste from the city in order to verify or determine the amounts which should be remitted to the city. Each commercial contractor shall make its books, records and computer data pertinent to the removal of solid waste from the city available for audit. If the results of any such audit show that any of the commercial contractor's reports understate the amount owing to the city, the underpayment shall be remitted to the city immediately, and if the understatement amounts to five percent or more, the commercial contractor shall also remit to the city a sum equal to ten percent of the underpayment, and shall also reimburse the city for its costs in conducting the audit.
(b) All permitted commercial contractors shall also submit such other reports as the director may reasonably require regarding the removal of solid waste from the city in order to provide information needed by the city to comply with applicable state and federal reporting requirements imposed upon the city. Solid waste refers to trash and to recycling, if the permitted hauler provides recycling services. All permitted commercial contractors shall provide quarterly information regarding tons landfilled and recycled to their city customers that are legally required to reduce their landfilled solid waste by 25 percent. This information shall be provided in a timely and accurate manner. Withholding of this information, delay in providing the information which causes the city customer to miss a legal deadline, or the providing of inaccurate information shall constitute a violation of this chapter and may result in fines, permit revocation, or both, as provided in sections 38-30 and 38-31.
(c) Every permitted commercial contractor is required to provide dependable solid waste service to customers within the city. Failure to provide dependable service may result in fines, permit revocation, or both, as provided in sections 38-30 and 38-31.
(Code 1989, § 11-83; Ord. No. 354, § 3, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 2, 5-3-1999; Ord. No. 455, § 1, 11-6-2000; Ord. No. 505, 9-23-2002)
898:
An adequate number of vehicles shall be provided by the commercial contractor to service its city customers. All such vehicles shall be licensed in the state and shall operate in compliance with all applicable state, federal and municipal regulations. All vehicles and other equipment shall be kept in proper repair and sanitary condition. Each vehicle shall have at least one broom and shovel to clean up solid waste that may be spilled or otherwise scattered during the process of collection. All vehicles shall be sufficiently secure so as to prevent any littering of solid waste and/or leakage of fluid. No vehicle shall be willfully overloaded. Each vehicle shall be operated by a qualified driver holding a valid license of the category required to operate such vehicles.
(Code 1989, § 11-84; Ord. No. 354, § 4, 12-19-1994)
899:
(a) Each commercial contractor shall provide and maintain, during the term of its permit, public liability and property damage insurance and umbrella coverage in such amounts as shall be reasonably determined from time to time by the director. The initial insurance requirements are as follows:
(1) Public liability:
a. $500,000.00 per person.
b. $1,000,000.00 per accident.
(2) Property damage: $500,000.00 per any one claim.
(3) Performance bond: varies according to number of city contracts.
(b) Each commercial contractor shall provide a certificate of such insurance to the city prior to undertaking collection services within the city, and, at each annual renewal of the permit, shall submit to the city an updated certificate of insurance together with the annual permit fee. Each commercial contractor shall defend, indemnify and save harmless and protect the city, its officers and agents, from any and all liability, loss or claims, actions, demands or judgments made against it for loss, damage or personal injury sustained by any person or entity whatsoever in connection with the services rendered by the commercial contractor, unless such damages are due to the negligence of the city, its officers, agents or employees.
(Code 1989, § 11-85; Ord. No. 354, § 5, 12-19-1994; Ord. No. 421, § 3, 5-3-1999)
900:
Each commercial contractor shall have a positive net worth and adequate capital and assets to perform its contracts with city customers. As a condition to the issuance of a permit, the director may require the submission of financial statements or similar information to verify these financial requirements. Any information submitted that is proprietary or constitutes a trade secret shall, subject to applicable law, be held confidential by the city.
(Code 1989, § 11-86; Ord. No. 354, § 6, 12-19-1994)
901:
Not less than ten days prior to commencing service, each commercial contractor shall furnish for the city's approval the initial schedules and maps of all routes to be used in servicing the commercial contractor's city customers. Any charges in routes and/or schedules shall also be subject to the director's approval, which will not be unreasonably withheld. The commercial contractor shall only undertake collections during the city's normal hours of collection, as adopted from time to time by the director. Exceptions may be made only upon the mutual agreement of the director and the commercial contractor. The commercial contractor shall also comply with all applicable city ordinances, including the city's noise provisions.
(Code 1989, § 11-87; Ord. No. 354, § 7, 12-19-1994)
902:
Any violation of this chapter by the commercial contractor may be punished according to the penalties described in section 1-8. Each day that a violation occurs shall constitute a separate offense. The city shall also have the right to initiate civil action to compel compliance with this chapter and to collect any unpaid permit fees.
(Code 1989, § 11-88; Ord. No. 354, § 8, 12-19-1994)
903:
If a commercial contractor fails to perform in accordance with this chapter or other applicable ordinances, the director shall have the right to demand, in writing, adequate assurance from the commercial contractor that steps have been taken to rectify the situation. The commercial contractor must, within seven days of receipt of such demand, return to the director a written statement that explains reasons for non-performance or delayed, partial or substandard performance, and provides adequate assurance as to future performance. In the event that the commercial contractor fails to submit a statement satisfactory to the director, the director may revoke the commercial contractor's permit. Such revocation shall become effective 30 days following a notice of revocation to the commercial contractor. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the right to continue to operate under a permit issued by the city is expressly conditioned upon the commercial contractor's timely payment of permit fees. Continued operation in the city without payment of such fees shall be unlawful. In addition, the city may revoke a permit for nonpayment of fees immediately and without notice.
(Code 1989, § 11-89; Ord. No. 354, § 9, 12-19-1994)
904:
(a) It is the policy and intent of the city that commercial and industrial refuse collection services are provided within the city on a competitive, free market basis. In order to promote this policy and intent, commercial and industrial customers within the city are encouraged to solicit multiple bids from qualified vendors for the provision of refuse collection services.
(b) In furtherance of this policy and intent, qualified vendors are encouraged to solicit commercial and industrial customers within the city for the purpose of providing commercial and industrial refuse collection services. It is also the policy and intent of the city that all qualified commercial and industrial vendors have free access to the market within the city, that all such vendors are afforded an equal opportunity to complete for and provide such services, and that no vendor shall be given preference over another.
(Code 1989, § 11-90; Res. No. 536, §§ 1, 2, 6-13-1994)

908:

(a) In order to ensure adequate illumination of public rights-of-way and promote safety and security, it is hereby ordained that the American National Standard Practice for Roadway Lighting of the Illuminating Engineering Society, as approved by the American National Standards Institute (1977), as amended, is hereby adopted as the standard for the installation and operation of lighting in the city, with the following exceptions:
(1) Lighting fixtures installed within the public rights-of-way to be operated for the purpose of street illumination shall comply with these standards. The minimum average horizontal footcandle illumination level by roadway classification shall be:
Roadway Classification | Commercial Area | Intermediate Area | Residential Area
Major thoroughfares | 2.0 | 1.2 | 0.9
Industrial parkways | 2.0 | 1.2 | 0.9
Collector streets | 1.2 | 0.9 | 0.6
Local and residential streets | 0.9 | 0.6 | 0.2
The uniformity of illumination shall be such that the point of lowest illumination shall have at least one-third of the average horizontal footcandle required illumination level, except that on local or residential streets, it may be not less than one-sixth of this average.
(2) Any party installing or operating lighting fixtures within a public right-of-way shall furnish plans and specifications to the city building official for approval showing how the proposed lighting meets the standards, and no lighting shall be installed or operated without this approval. Should the city building official disapprove the request to install or operate lighting fixtures within any public right-of-way, such official shall communicate the disapproval in writing to the party desiring the same. The written communication shall include the specific reasons for disapproval. Any disapproval of a light or lighting system by the city building official may be appealed to the city council. If any party desires to appeal an adverse decision by the building official, a notice of appeal shall be filed with the city council within 30 days from the date following the written notice of disapproval, and it shall be the responsibility of the city building official to transmit forthwith to the city council all papers and allied documents constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken and to ensure that the appeal is promptly placed upon the agenda of the city council at its next regularly scheduled meeting. The city council may reverse or affirm, wholly or partly, or may modify the order, requirement, decision or determination appealed from.
(3) Roadway or street lighting luminaries or fixtures installed within the public right-of-way as security lights or for the purpose of lighting areas other than the public streets shall be mounted on the side of the pole opposite the street side and shall be oriented in such a manner as to ensure that the lateral light distribution pattern is parallel to the street and the vertical light distribution, at the initial light source, is perpendicular to the street, so as to protect the users of the street from objectionable glare. The approval of the city building official shall be obtained before installation of these lights.
(4) Other lighting fixtures to be installed within or outside of public right-of-way for whatever purpose shall be installed and operated in such a manner to prevent glare from being a hazard to or interfering with the normal use of the public right-of-way.

The dedication and acceptance for perpetual maintenance of public improvements shall be effected in the following manner:
(1) Prior to the construction of a public improvement, the developer shall submit a detailed site plan of the proposed development, including all public improvements. The detailed site plan shall specify the location of all street lights, and the developer shall submit proof of payment for pole and electrical installation. The plans shall conform in all respects to the city standard construction specifications and standard plans in effect at the time the plans are submitted.
(2) Prior to the construction of such public improvements, the developer shall post a performance bond with the city conditioned upon the faithful performance and completion of the public improvements by the developer. The performance bond shall be in an amount equal to the estimated cost of the public improvements, as determined in the sole discretion of the director of community development. The performance bond shall be issued by a surety authorized to do business in the state and certified by the Department of the Treasury as an acceptable surety on federal bonds. The developer shall notify the director of community development when the construction of the improvements has been completed, and the director of community development shall inspect the improvements to determine if construction has been completed in compliance with city standards. If the director of community development determines that the construction of the improvements has been completed in accordance with city standards, the director of community development shall notify the developer in writing of such determination, and the developer shall promptly post a maintenance bond with the city conditioned upon the developer's maintenance of the improvements for a period of one year. The bond shall be in the amount of one-third of the estimated cost of the improvements; provided, however, that if the developer has previously failed to comply with any provision of this article, the city may require that the amount of the bond be equal to 43 percent of the estimated cost of improvements. At such time as the city has received the required maintenance bond, the city shall release the performance bond. The surety issuing the maintenance bond shall have the same qualifications as the surety issuing the performance bond. The director of community development's inspection and approval of the improvements, and the city's release of the performance bond, shall not constitute a warranty by the city that the improvements have been completed in accordance with all city standards. During the period of the one-year maintenance bond, the director of community development and representatives of other city departments shall have the right to conduct periodic inspections of the improvements, including the taking of core samples and the performing of other tests as the director of community development deems appropriate. The cost of the core sampling shall be borne by the developer.
(3) Not sooner than 75 days nor later than 60 days prior to the expiration of the one-year maintenance bond, the developer shall petition the city to accept the public improvements for perpetual maintenance. Failure to petition the city shall result in forfeiture of the maintenance bond. Upon receipt of the petition, the director of community development shall notify the fire department, police department, department of community development and the public works department. Each department shall conduct inspections of the improvements and shall submit reports to the director of community development on forms and within time deadlines established by the director of community development. The director of community development, through his own inspection and by the reports submitted by the city departments referred to above, shall be responsible for determining if the improvements are in accordance with city standards and are otherwise acceptable for perpetual maintenance. If the director of community development finds that the improvements are deficient in any respect, the director of community development shall so notify the developer and the developer shall timely perform such additional work as the director of community development deems necessary to render the improvements acceptable for perpetual maintenance by the city. The failure of the developer to timely perform the work specified by the director of community development shall result in forfeiture of the maintenance bond. Upon the director of community development's final determination that the improvements are acceptable by the city for perpetual maintenance, the director of community development shall so notify the developer in writing, and the maintenance bond shall be released. Notwithstanding the release of the performance bond or maintenance bond, the developer shall have the responsibility of maintaining all improvements until such time as the director of community development has issued the city's written acceptance for perpetual maintenance of the improvements.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms shall mean:
Illegal street racing and reckless driving exhibition means a motor vehicle speed contest using public highways, streets, or rights-of-way in violation of applicable motor vehicle and traffic laws, including without limitation, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-186, § 40-6-251 and § 40-6-390. Illegal street racing and reckless driving exhibitions may include, but are not limited to, situations in which:
(1) A group of motor vehicles or individuals has arrived at a location for the purpose of participating in the event;
(2) A group of individuals has gathered on private property open to the general public without the consent of the owner, operator, or agent thereof for the purpose of participating in the event;
(3) One or more individuals has impeded the free public use of a public street, sidewalk or highway by actions, words, or physical barriers for the purpose of conducting the event;
(4) Two or more vehicles have lined up with motors running for an illegal motor vehicle speed contest or exhibition of speed;
(5) One or more drivers is revving his engine or spinning his tires in preparation for the event;
(6) An individual is stationed at or near one or more motor vehicles serving as a race starter; or
(7) One or more vehicles causing damage due to swinging, drifting, or racing.
Organizer means any individual who in any manner knowingly takes part in the planning, organization, coordination, facilitation, advertising, publicizing, or sharing of the location for any such illegal street race, collecting moneys in connection with, or videoing an illegal street racing exhibition as defined herein.

1134:
No permit is required if the operation of the taxicab in the city is limited solely to passing through the city without picking up a passenger or dropping off a passenger whose trip originated outside the city.
(Code 1989, § 13-147; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 1, 3-3-2003)
1135:
There shall be three classes of permits required under this article:
(1) Company permit. This permit applies to persons, firms, partnerships, corporations or other entities engaged in the business of operating a taxicab in the city, and which are subject to an occupation tax under chapter 42.
(2) Resident operator's permit. This permit applies to any person operating a taxicab on the streets of the city and who is operating under the auspices of a company permit.
(3) Nonresident operator's permit. This permit applies to any person operating a taxicab on the streets of the city and who is not operating under the auspices of a company subject to an occupation tax in the city.
(Code 1989, § 13-148; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1137:
No permit shall be issued if the applicant has been convicted of any of the following offenses:
(1) Manslaughter, or negligent homicide, resulting from the operation of a motor vehicle.
(2) Driving a motor vehicle while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs, in the last five years.
(3) Any felony in the commission of which a motor vehicle is used.
(4) Failure to stop and render aid or leaving the scene of an accident, as required under the laws of the state.
(5) Perjury or false swearing in making any statements under oath in connection with this application for permit.
(6) Perjury or the making of a false affidavit or statement under oath relating to the ownership or operation of motor vehicles.
(7) Convictions or forfeiture of bail on three charges of a violation of the state motor vehicle laws within a 12-month period.
(8) The violation of any law involving moral turpitude.
(9) Repeated violation of the city ordinances, county laws, or state laws which affect the safety of human life or limb on the streets of the city.
(Code 1989, § 13-150; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 2, 3-3-2003)
1138:
No person to whom an occupation tax certificate to operate or engage in a taxicab business has been granted by lawful authority shall operate or carry on the business from any place in the city except the established place of business referred to and described in the application for an occupation tax certificate to operate or engage in the taxicab business.
(Code 1989, § 13-151; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1139:
The standard hours of operations for any holder of a company permit to operate or engage in a taxicab business within the city shall be Monday through Sunday, 24 hours per day.
(Code 1989, § 13-152; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1140:
(a) No owner of a taxicab shall operate or authorize any other person to operate a taxicab in the city unless it is covered by a liability insurance policy issued by an insurance company authorized to do business in this state, which provides the following minimum coverage:
(1) $25,000.00 for injury to or death of one person in one accident;
(2) $50,000.00 for injury to or death of two or more persons in any one accident; and
(3) $25,000.00 for injury or destruction of property of others in any one accident.
(b) Each taxicab operated within the city limits shall be required to carry and maintain in effect this minimum insurance coverage and provide current certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage, the name of the insurance company supplying the coverage and the policy number. The insurance must provide specific coverage for a vehicle used in the business of transporting passengers.
(c) If the term of said insurance coverage is less than a period of 12 months, on the first Monday of each month, the holder of the company permit shall provide to the chief of police or his designee either a current insurance identification card for each vehicle intended to be operated in the coming month or a verified statement from a licensed insurance agent or licensed insurance company within this state setting forth the identity of the vehicles for which coverage has been procured, by vehicle identification number, make and model, the amount of coverage afforded to each such vehicle and the term for which such coverage has been prepared by the taxicab company or taxicab driver.
(d) If the term of such insurance coverage is at least a period of 12 months, proof of such insurance coverage, together with a receipted premium from the insurer, or its duly authorized agent, showing payment of the premium on the policy for and during the period covered by the life of the occupational tax certificate, shall be provided to the city before a permit shall be issued. The insurance policy must provide and stipulate therein that the insurer will give notice to the city a minimum of 30 days before its termination or cancellation, for any reason, of the policy on the person insured.
(e) Failure to maintain such coverage shall constitute cause for revocation of a city permit.
(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive applicable state or federal laws, if any, which require a higher amount of minimum coverage.
(Code 1989, § 13-153; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 3, 3-3-2003)
1142:
All taxicabs operating in the city shall:
(1) Be equipped with a taximeter maintained in good working order at all times. Such taximeter shall be permanently affixed in front of the passenger's seat and be visible to them at all times. After sundown, the face of the taximeter shall be illuminated. It shall be operated mechanically by a mechanism of standard design and construction, driven either from the transmission or from one of the front wheels by a flexible and permanently attached driving mechanism. It shall be sealed at all points and connections that, if manipulated, would affect its correct reading and recording.
(2) Be affixed with a vehicle permit sticker issued by the director of public safety or his designee. Such stickers must at all times be displayed in the upper right corner of the rear window. Each vehicle will be assigned a numbered sticker, and that sticker shall not be used on any other vehicle.
(3) Such marking shall be affixed only by means of permanent vinyl lettering or paint, and shall be a minimum of four inches in height. The four-inch lettering requirement can be met if the logo is a minimum of four inches in height and the lettering within the logo is a minimum of two inches in height.
(4) Be marked with rates on the side of the vehicle so as to be plainly visible to persons seeking to use the taxicab.
(5) Maintain signage in the passenger compartment stating, in clearly legible lettering of a minimum of one inch in height, "The public is invited to contact the city department of public safety by calling (678)297-6306 to report any instance of a taxicab being operated while not in a clean and safe operating condition."
(6) Be equipped with a roof light permanently mounted on the roof of the vehicle and maintained in good working order at all times.
(7) Be maintained in good, safe and serviceable mechanical condition as verified in a statement signed by a technician at a location properly licensed to do business within the city, and be in compliance with all county and state licensing and emission standards.
(8) Be maintained in a clean condition, free from foreign matter and offensive odors.
(9) Transport as passengers only the number of persons specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
(10) The minimum weight of a taxicab shall be 2,000 pounds, as determined by the manufacturer's specifications.
(11) No vehicle operated as a taxicab shall be more than eight years old.
(12) No taxicab shall have less than three doors for loading passengers, and each taxicab must be a station wagon, a sedan, a minivan or a sports utility vehicle. All such vehicles shall meet the emission standards as set by federal guidelines for their particular class.
(Code 1989, § 13-155; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 5, 3-3-2003)
1143:
(a) Daily trip sheets shall be maintained for all taxicabs operated within the city. The driver shall retain the trip sheets in the vehicle for a period of 72 hours from the time of the recorded trip, after which they will be maintained in the office of the company permit holder for a period of no less than 120 days. All trip sheets shall be subject to the inspection of the police chief or his designee.
(b) As used in this subsection, the term "trip sheet" means a daily log of all passengers, the time, place of entry and the destination of each passenger, the amount charged and an itemization of any personal property left in the vehicle for hire.
(Code 1989, § 13-156; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1144:
Any vehicle permit issued in accordance with this article shall not be transferable.
(Code 1989, § 13-157; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1145:
(a) An application for a permit or a permit issued under this article may be denied, suspended or revoked for due cause as defined in subsection (c) of this section.
(b) The municipal court shall furnish a permit holder a notice setting forth the time, place, and purpose of a hearing at which it intends to consider the revocation or suspension of a permit. After a hearing, if the municipal court determines due cause exists, it may suspend, revoke or place on probation for a maximum of 12 months, with or without conditions, the permit.
(c) A permit may be denied, suspended or revoked for any of the following reasons:
(1) Where the applicant furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information or omits information requested in the application for a permit.
(2) For failure to pay all fees, taxes, penalties or other charges imposed by the provisions of this article, and of this Code.
(3) For failure to maintain all of the general qualifications applicable to the initial issuance of a permit.
(4) For violation of any part of this article by the permit holder, his agents, partners, officers, employees or contractors.
(5) Allowing the required insurance coverage to lapse shall result in the automatic suspension of the permit.
(6) For unauthorized transfer or other misuse of the permit.
(d) An operator's permit may be suspended or revoked for having three or more moving violations in any 12-month period.
(e) Permit holders under this article are responsible for violations of this article by their vehicle operators whether such operators are direct employees or independent contractors.
(f) Permits issued under this article are not transferable.
(Code 1989, § 13-158; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 6, 3-3-2003)
1146:
A regulatory fee of $300.00 shall be required annually for a company permit and the resident operator's permits for drivers operating under the auspices of a company permit. A regulatory fee of $50.00 shall be required annually for a nonresident operator's permit.
(Code 1989, § 13-159; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002; Ord. No. 523, § 7, 3-3-2003)
1147:
It shall be the duty of a company permit holder to notify the director of public safety whenever a new driver is hired or terminated from employment. Failure to so notify can result in revocation of the permit.
(Code 1989, § 13-160; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1149:
(a) The police department and the code enforcement office shall enforce the regulations contained in this article.
(b) Violations of the provisions of this article shall be punished according to the penalties described in section 1-8. Each separate occurrence shall be deemed a separate offense.
(c) The violation of the provisions of this article by any person, corporation, partnership or other entity may be enjoined by instituting appropriate proceedings for injunction in the courts of competent jurisdiction in this state. Such actions may be maintained notwithstanding that other adequate remedies at law exist. Such actions may be instituted in the name of the city.
(d) Violations of any provision of this article by any permit holder shall be due cause for revocation of any city permit or certificate, after notice and hearing before the city municipal court.
(Code 1989, § 13-162; Ord. No. 497, § I, 6-17-2002)
1150:
Nothing in this article shall be deemed to prohibit the charging of a flat rate for trips to and from Hartsfield International Airport, provided that such flat rates are conspicuously posted on the taxicab or set forth on a rate card provided to the customer prior to the trip.
(Code 1989, § 13-163; Ord. No. 523, § 9, 3-3-2003)
